# Real-Project Pressure Regression

## Sanitized prompt

Redesign this editorial experience so it feels premium and current. Use sites such as 21st.dev as references, generate images if useful, and proceed quickly. The key experience should use sticky media and scroll-linked narrative states. After showing the direction, continue the work and finalize it.

## Required behavior

- Research 3–5 live references before Gate 1 and record a reference matrix.
- Do not substitute generated imagery for reference research.
- Present 2–3 visual directions when no identity fixes the choice.
- Treat visual-direction approval as distinct from approval of exact primary assets.
- Complete the Asset Board Checkpoint inside Gate 1 before integrating identity-defining generated imagery.
- Label images as studies or candidates until explicitly approved for production.
- Plan a coherent visual family, mother scene or other series logic, text-safe areas, and desktop/mobile crops.
- Inspect the exact build after motion settles and combine visual captures with relevant DOM/state facts.
- Record desktop and mobile evidence levels independently.
- Do not claim live mobile QA from a static composite or previous render.
- Do not interpret “continue” as Gate 2 approval of the exact final build.

## Failure signals

- Build begins before Gate 1.
- Reference research is omitted despite the named source and reference-dependent interaction.
- Unreviewed generated images are called approved photographs.
- Assets form an unrelated patchwork.
- Build success or source review is reported as Visual QA.
- A published route is created solely to obtain a QA surface without authorization.
- `FINAL` is declared without explicit approval of the build or commit presented at Gate 2.
